svg.title: K4 — Shuttle mat: mechanisms
svg.text: K4 — Shuttle mat: how the mechanisms work
Section views, simplified; each panel loops on its own. Numbers from the concept document [E].

g.text: cassette K; S, D, P, R wait
Five mats stay wound on their own driven reels under the table. Bar
B fetches the hem of the wanted mat and draws it out through the
wash gate; afterwards the reel winds it back through the same gate.
Mat exchange and mat wash are one motion.
5 cassettes K S D P R · 75–100 s exchange incl. wash
2 Dicing on the mat: slab, strip, chop
mat K on the soft anvil strip
No dicing grid: the blade chops slabs while the mat jogs, the roller
levels them to one layer, a disc-knife roller cuts strips in one
pass, the blade chops again. It also dices raw meat. Unproven (risk
R4); a die head is the fallback.
3 LOOP: the slack mat as a trough
bar B moves in, reels pay out slack
reels reverse: the trough rolls the mince
loop closes, log back on the table
Bar B comes close to the table edge and the reels pay out
slack: the mat hangs between two cheeks as a trough. When reel
and bar wind the same way, its wall moves and the charge
tumbles; mince or dough rolls into a log of set diameter.
cheeks 300 × 320 · log Ø 60 · 12 patties in 3 min
4 ENVELOPE: tools work through the mat
cutlet: no contact with the roller
bar B folds the mat back over the cutlet
roller works on the back of the mat
Arm B carries the free end of the mat back over the food, so the
roller presses on the mat, not on the food (the cook's cling-film
method). Then the mat is peeled off at 150–180°: sticky mince or
dough never touches a roller and needs no flour.
5 SLING and NOSE: carry, then lay down
SLING: the free span carries the sheet
NOSE: bar moves back and winds in
sheet laid flat on the tray
speed of travel = speed of winding
The mat spans freely from the table edge to bar B and is the only
conveyor for solids, to every hob, tin and tray. To lay down, bar B
travels back over the target while winding in: the mat is pulled
from under the food. A doctor lip keeps sticky film off the bar.
bar reach 850 mm radius · pizza sheet 380 × 290 × 4
6 Washed while it is wound back: the gate
mat comes down from the table
Both faces of every square centimetre pass every nozzle row at 40
mm, so coverage is by construction (not for lip roots, hem and mesh
holes). Silicone, mesh and rasp mats take the steam slot; mat K
stops three times for 60 s in the 85 °C rinse after raw meat.
2.5 m mat in 100 s · ≈ 1.6 L water + 30 g steam per pass
